The zampogna is the general name for several kinds of double-chanter bagpipe around Lazio in Italy, an aerophone with the Hornbostel–Sachs number 422.122-7+422.122-62. The chanter and the drone are fixed into a single round stock, which is joined to the bag; the double-reed version usually has a treble pipe on the right, a bass pipe on the left and an alto drone, while the single-reed version has a short-pipe form and variants from Sicily and southern Calabria. The double-reed version is usually played with the piffero (a folk double-reed oboe) to provide harmony, rhythm or bass; the single-reed version can be played solo. It is traditionally associated with Christmas and also appears at folk music festivals.
「義大利風笛」一詞源自拉丁文「symphonia」，詞源與希臘文「sumphōn: The word zampogna comes from the Latin 'symphonia', related in etymology to the Greek 'sumphōnía', meaning 'harmony or a unison of sounds', formed from 'syn-' (together, at the same time) and 'phōnḗ' (sound), which later came to name a kind of bagpipe. It shares its origin with the Greek island bagpipe 'tsampouna', which is itself a reborrowing of 'zampogna'. It is also related to a Romanian word meaning 'symphony' or 'many sounds played at once', and to the Georgian and Spanish 'zampoña' (the Andean panpipe) and similar words. These connections show how widely the zampogna has shaped the musical cultures of the Mediterranean and beyond.

The double-reed version is usually played with the piffero (a shawm or folk oboe): the piffero plays the melody while the zampogna provides chords, rhythmic harmony, a bass line or treble harmony. The single-reed version can play alone, as the surdullina does, mainly playing the tarantella, and the ciaramedda plays traditional regional melodies.

The traditional bag is a whole goatskin or sheepskin with the hair left inside; bags are now also made from rubber inner tube or from synthetic material covered with artificial hair. The blowpipe has a simple leather valve. A keyed Lucanian example has a bell and stock of maple and a chanter bore of olive, and an oilcloth bag and a synthetic-resin mouthpiece that appear to have been added later. The other parts are not stated.

義大利風笛的音色具有溫暖而粗獷的特質，帶有濃厚的民族色彩。其音色介於明亮與暗沉之: The zampogna's timbre is warm and rough-hewn, with a strong regional character. It lies between bright and dark, giving off a warm, weathered quality full of a desolate poetry. The instrument is built with two pipes and can sound melody and accompaniment at once, with a wide range in several layers: the bass is warm and deep, the middle and upper registers relatively sharp and penetrating. Its resonance depends on the steady supply of air from the bag and the resonating chambers of the pipes, producing a continuous, even sound. Compared with the Scottish bagpipe the zampogna is gentler and more intimate; compared with modern instruments it keeps more of an original, rustic flavour, with a strong local character and a sense of history.
